learning_objective: 🎯 Step out of the flat 2D page and enter the real world! Learn to plot points, calculate distances, and divide line segments in 3D space using X, Y, and Z coordinates.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔀 The X, Y, and Z Axes
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In 2D, you have left-right (X) and up-down (Y). In 3D, we add forward-backward (Z). These three mutually perpendicular axes intersect at the Origin $(0,0,0)$. Every point in space is located using three coordinates: $(x, y, z)$.

In 2D, the X and Y axes divide the plane into 4 Quadrants. In 3D, the X, Y, and Z axes divide the entire space into 8 rooms or blocks, called Octants. The signs of the coordinates (+ or -) determine exactly which octant a point is sitting in.
The distance between two points $P(x_1, y_1, z_1)$ and $Q(x_2, y_2, z_2)$ is a direct expansion of the 2D Pythagoras theorem: $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2 + (z_2 - z_1)^2}$.

If a point $R$ divides the line segment joining $P(x_1, y_1, z_1)$ and $Q(x_2, y_2, z_2)$ in the ratio $m:n$, the coordinates of $R$ are: $(\frac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m+n}, \frac{my_2 + ny_1}{m+n}, \frac{mz_2 + nz_1}{m+n})$ for internal division.

fun_activity.title: 🧊 The Room Corner Coordinates
fun_activity.instructions: Look at one of the bottom corners of the room you are sitting in. Imagine that corner is the Origin (0,0,0). The line where the floor meets the wall to your right is the X-axis. The line meeting the wall to your left is the Y-axis. The vertical corner line going to the ceiling is the Z-axis. A fly hovering right in the middle of the room has (x, y, z) coordinates!

exam_tips: 📌 Any point lying on the X-axis will have the coordinates $(x, 0, 0)$. Any point on the YZ-plane will have its x-coordinate as zero: $(0, y, z)$.
📌 To find the ratio in which a specific plane (like the XY-plane) cuts a line segment, assume the ratio is $k:1$, set the missing coordinate (Z-coordinate for XY-plane) to 0, and solve for $k$.

📌 The coordinates of the Centroid of a triangle with vertices $(x_1,y_1,z_1)$, $(x_2,y_2,z_2)$, and $(x_3,y_3,z_3)$ are simply the averages: $(\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3}{3}, \frac{y_1+y_2+y_3}{3}, \frac{z_1+z_2+z_3}{3})$.
quick_recap: ⭐ Space is divided into 8 octants by the XY, YZ, and ZX planes.
⭐ For external division in the section formula, simply replace the '+' signs with '-' signs.
⭐ The distance of a point $P(x,y,z)$ from the origin is $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}$.
